quotes.t: Happiness is a good flow of life.
We have two ears and one mouth, so we should listen more than we say.
quotes.c: As quoted in Diogenes Laërtius Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, vii. 23.

quotes.t: (The end is) life in agreement with nature
quotes.c: As quoted by Diogenes Laërtius, in Lives of Eminent Philosophers: 'Zeno', 7.87.: "This is why Zeno was the first (in his treatise On the Nature of Man) to designate as the end 'life in agreement with nature' (or living agreeably to nature)..." The "end" here means "the goal of life."

quotes.t: A bad feeling is a commotion of the mind repugnant to reason, and against nature.
quotes.c: As quoted in Tusculanae Quaestiones by Cicero, iv. 6.

quotes.t: All the good are friends of one another.
quotes.c: As quoted in Stromata, v. 14. by Clement of Alexandria

quotes.t: If melodiously piping flutes sprang from the olive, would you doubt that a knowledge of flute-playing resided in the olive? And what if plane trees bore harps which gave forth rhythmical sounds? Clearly you would think in the same way that the art of music was possessed by plane trees. Why, then, seeing that the universe gives birth to beings that are animate and wise, should it not be considered animate and wise itself?
quotes.c: As quoted in De Natura Deorum by Cicero, ii. 8.

quotes.t: Love is a God, who cooperates in securing the safety of the city.
quotes.c: As quoted in Deipnosophists by Athenaeus, xiii. 561c.

quotes.t: No evil is honorable; but death is honorable; therefore death is not evil.
quotes.c: As quoted in Epistles No. 82, by Seneca the Younger

quotes.t: No one entrusts a secret to a drunken man; but one will entrust a secret to a good man; therefore, the good man will not get drunk.
quotes.c: As quoted in Epistulae morales ad Lucilium by Seneca, Epistle LXXXIII (trans. R. M. Gummere)

quotes.t: That which exercises reason is more excellent than that which does not exercise reason; there is nothing more excellent than the universe, therefore the universe exercises reason.
quotes.c: As quoted in De Natura Deorum by Cicero, ii. 8.; iii. 9.

quotes.t: If thou wishest to be a philosopher, learn first to die.
It is the hallmark of the cultivated man that he can live in any society; the narrow-souled man, on the other hand, can live only in some.
Life which is not examined is not worth living.
Nature does nothing in vain.
No one is free who is not master of himself.
No one is rich whose virtual wealth can be counted.
The end of life is rest, and rest is our chief good.
The foundation of all inquiry is wonder.
The foundation of every state is the education of its youth.
The goal of life is living in agreement with nature.
The good and wise man is only happy.
The happy man is the one who has no fear of death.
The nature of an obstacle is to be overcome. What's in the way becomes the way.
The only way to comprehend what lies in front of you is to let go of what lies behind.
The wise man is always happy.
The wise man is not a slave to his body.
The wise man is not a slave to his country.
The wise man is not a slave to his enemies.
The wise man is not a slave to his friends.
The wise man is not a slave to his gods.
The wise man is not a slave to his passions.
The wise man is not a slave to his possessions.
The wise man is not a slave to his reputation.
The wise man is not afraid of death.
The wise man is not angry with men, but pities them.
The wise man is not moved by the vicissitudes of fortune.
The wise man is poor when he has nothing, and rich when he has something.
The wise man is self-sufficient, for all goods are within him.
Virtue is nothing else than the state of a soul in harmony.
We are more likely to act ourselves into a new way of thinking than to think ourselves into a new way of acting.
We are not born once and for all on the day our mother gives birth to us, but life obliges us to give birth to ourselves throughout our life.
We must believe in luck. For how else can we explain the success of those we don't like?
We should every night retire to bed with the reflection that we have lived another day in innocence and justice.
Well-being is realized by small steps and not by leaps and bounds.
Well-being is realized by virtue, circumstance does not affect it at all.
